name: x3d-stem-turing-garden/v1
purpose: Turing Garden (x3d.STEM flagship 2). Accepting under it means: the scene is grammatical and meaningful on the fork with no known trap; all five gardens declare their model and limits; the exact linear-mode, budget-identity, convergence-order, reproducibility and maximum-principle witnesses are green; every frame's reference mesh is closed, its volume agrees with the field, the published precision moves the surface less than the declared limit, and each garden's name is a measured claim; payloads inflate to their recorded bytes; the builder and the solver module are the shipped ones; and a browser rebuilt every mesh from the verified fields and matched the builder's reference, with playback following the scene's own TimeSensor route.
limitations: Page traps are static pattern and syntax checks of src/*.js against the X_ITE contracts the Loom has paid for (law 32); the page's browser evidence remains the behaviour witness.
Behaviour is one headless Chromium on one machine (Apple M3, ANGLE Metal): mesh counts and volumes and playback order, not pixels or frame rate.
No offline-render comparison of browser frames (eyes) for this study yet.
The shared library lib/stemkit lies outside the candidate; its hashes are recorded in each case (external_dependencies) but not gated.
Grammar and Meaning ran on the local x3d_mcp fork checkout, not the family pin.
Unsigned receipt: it shows drift; it does not authenticate authorship.
